question: A 3-week-old male is brought to the emergency department because of increasing lethargy. He was born at home without prenatal care or neonatal screening and appeared to be normal at birth. Despite this, his parents noticed that he would vomit after breastfeeding. He then progressively became more lethargic and began to have a few episodes of diarrhea after feeding. His parents do not recall any significant family history and neither of his siblings have had similar symptoms. Upon presentation, the infant is found to be generally unresponsive with mild hepatomegaly. Physical exam further reveals signs of clouding in the lenses of his eyes bilaterally. The levels of which of the following metabolites will be most dramatically elevated in this patient?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Galactose" -> "Galactose-1-phosphate" -> "Galactose-1-phosphate accumulation due to enzyme deficiency" -> "Elevated galactose-1-phosphate levels in the patient" -> 95%
CHAIN: "Galactose-1-phosphate" -> "Inhibition of glycolysis" -> "Impaired energy production" -> "Lethargy and hepatomegaly in the patient" -> 90%
analysis: Based on the clinical presentation of the infant with lethargy, vomiting after breastfeeding, diarrhea, clouding in the lenses of the eyes, and hepatomegaly, along with the absence of prenatal care and neonatal screening, the most likely diagnosis is galactosemia. Galactosemia is an inborn error of metabolism where there is a deficiency of the enzyme galactose-1-phosphate uridyltransferase, leading to the accumulation of galactose-1-phosphate. This accumulation can result in various symptoms including liver dysfunction, cataracts, and intellectual disability.
